content: The University Center at Nova Southeastern University is a 366,000 square-foot facility that plays a pivotal role in the university's infrastructure. Its construction spanned two years, and it officially opened with an inaugural event featuring comedian Jamie Kennedy on August 23, 2006. The center serves as a central hub for campus life, offering a venue for students, faculty, staff, and the community to attend guest lectures, concerts, sporting events, galas, and other activities. The Arena The arena within the University Center is highly versatile and can be configured to suit various events and sports. It has a seating capacity of over 4,500 guests. The space can be transformed into a concert venue, a convocation center, a gathering area for university-wide activities, a family entertainment venue, or a site for intercollegiate athletics. It is the home of NSU’s Sharks Men’s and Women’s Basketball teams, the Women’s Volleyball team, and the Athletic Department. The facility includes locker rooms, equipment rooms, and a team lounge, among other amenities. The arena is equipped with state-of-the-art sports medicine and athletic training facilities for NSU’s 250 student-athletes. These include advanced modalities such as ultrasound, electrical stimulation, diathermy, and a wide range of rehabilitation equipment. Notably, it features the only HydroWorx Aquatic Therapy and Fitness Pool in the tri-county area. The arena is managed by SMG Management Inc., a leading facilities management firm. Its current nickname is The Shark Tank, but naming rights are available for purchase at a price of $10 million. RecPlex Fitness Center The RecPlex Fitness Center, which replaced a former converted double-wide trailer, is a cornerstone of the campus recreation department. Membership is free for current students, while faculty, alumni, and the general public can join for varying fees. The RecPlex boasts 98 pieces of Star Trac cardiovascular equipment, 84 pieces of Star Trac strength equipment, a two-court multipurpose gym for basketball, volleyball, dodgeball, and more, as well as three multipurpose studios for group exercise and martial arts. Additional features include three indoor racquetball courts (one convertible to a squash court), a heated outdoor swimming pool, a 27-foot indoor rock climbing wall, personal training and massage therapy services, and men’s and women’s locker rooms with showers and saunas. The Student Union The University Center also houses the office of the Student Union, which aims to enrich and support the educational and social experiences of the university community. The Student Union organizes special events both on and off campus. Off-campus events include annual trips to the Florida Keys, Disney World, and local sporting events such as Miami Dolphins or Florida Panthers games. The Flight Deck The Flight Deck derives its name from the site’s historical use as a Navy airbase during World War II, where aircraft practiced takeoffs and landings on the short “Flight Deck” of U.S. Naval carriers. Additionally, NSU is located directly under the flight path of Fort Lauderdale International Airport. The Flight Deck features a serving bar with a beer and wine license, affordable snacks, pool tables, ping pong tables, large plasma TVs, and a gaming area. It hosts weekly activities, student events, happy hours, and union sports tournaments in games such as billiards, tennis, darts, dominoes, spades, and sports quiz bowls. The Flight Deck is also a venue for student organizations to host special events and is managed by the Student Union. Performing Arts Center The University Arts Center, located in the north wing of the facility, officially opened in January 2007. It includes a 300-seat performance theater, a multipurpose black box theater with roll-out seating that matches the stage layout of the Miniaci Theater, a professional-grade scene shop, and a gallery for displaying private art collections, photography, and student artwork. Additional amenities include choral and instrumental rehearsal rooms, six practice studios, and labs for acoustic, percussion, and keyboard technology.
